items.claim: The admonition_unit boundary at 24:21-22 is correctly warranted by the vocative-plus-motive grammar, and the single-witness setumah closing verse 22 is accurately disclosed and correctly tier-3.
items.evidence: 24:21 opens with the vocative-imperative sequence (skeleton tokens confirmed against oshb:Prov.24.21 byte text: יְרָֽא ... בְּנִ֣י), matching prov_device_inventory.json's bni_address list (Prov.24.21 is one of the isolated post-ch7 sites in the E-1 corrected 22-verse count, not the stale 17 figure). oshb:Prov.24.22 carries the book's one SAMEKH (pmarks_Prov.json: 51 PE + 1 SAMEKH over 52 verses total, the SAMEKH digit = 1, sited only at Prov.24.22), single-witness tier-3, correctly disclosed as corroboration rather than driver. rejected_alternative correctly names the only real rival (24:22 opening C4) and defeats it on the motive-clause dependency; the row does not overreach.

items.claim: The 24:23-25 proverb_cluster is warranted, and independently checking the bytes turns up a confirming inclusio the row itself never cites, strengthening rather than weakening the call.
items.evidence: Verse-final skeleton token at 24:23 and at 24:25 is the identical טוב/טוב ('not good' opening the header-maxim; 'blessing of good' closing v25) -- an undisclosed tov-inclusio bracketing exactly this row's three verses (v24 carries no tov token, so the bracket is clean, checked against consonantal_index.json). This sits alongside the row's own cited evidence (the case-illustration in v24 and the adversative construction opening v25) as additional, uncited support. rejected_alternative (splitting the header 23 from the illustration 24-25) is the genuine strongest rival and is properly defeated: 23 states a complete maxim rather than a bare label.

items.claim: The row's claim that 24:29 'shares no root' with the sluggard's-field vignette at 24:30 is bytes-false, and rejected_alternative never tests the stronger backward-merge rival with 24:28.
items.evidence: consonantal_index.json skeleton for Prov.24.29 ends with לאיש (the root man with a lamed prefix, 'to the man') and Prov.24.30 opens with the bare איש ('a man'); sweep.py --skel איש returns both verses among its book-wide hits, so the root recurs immediately across this row's closing seam, undisclosed -- exactly the cross-seam-cohesion class the toolkit flags as live in 10-29. Separately, rejected_alternative only tests a forward merge with the sluggard poem; it never engages the more textually grounded backward candidate: Prov.24.28 and Prov.24.29 both open with the identical אל/אל prohibition construction and both concern wronging a person (false testimony / private revenge), a construction-run class the book strategy elsewhere credits as legitimate cluster glue. The single_proverb verdict likely still survives (24:29 is a quoted forbidden speech-act, a different register from both neighbors), but the row's stated grounds for it are inaccurate and its rival-testing is incomplete.

items.claim: The wisdom_poem boundary at 24:30-34 is well warranted: the first-person narrative frame, the threefold refrain, and the single-witness petuchah closing both the unit and the C4 appendix all check out against the bytes.
items.evidence: Prov.24.33 skeleton carries the token מעט three times (verified via consonantal_index.json), confirming the row's threefold-refrain claim exactly. pmarks_Prov.json confirms Prov.24.34 = ['PE'], single-witness, correctly disclosed, and 24:34 is indeed the last verse of C4 per the book strategy's collection map, so the corroboration-not-driver framing is accurate. rejected_alternative (splitting a narrative pair 30-32 from a refrain-plus-application pair 33-34) is a genuine, non-strawman rival, correctly defeated because v33's refrain has no subject without the sluggard the narrative introduces.

items.claim: The 25:2-3 proverb_cluster is correctly grounded: the plural token and the shared root both recur across exactly these two verses and nowhere else in the part, verified against a full occurrence sweep.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel מלכים (plural 'kings') returns 7 verses book-wide; filtered to part P11 (25:1-27:27) only Prov.25.2 and Prov.25.3 fall inside, matching the row's claimed digit exactly. The shared root is realized as the infinitive חקר in v2 and the noun חקר in v3, confirmed by direct byte comparison. The contrast the row draws with the singular מלך at 25:1/25:5/25:6 (historical/royal-court referents, a different object from the plural) is bytes-accurate.

items.claim: The row's core cluster evidence (the shared imperative occurring at only 2 sites in the part, both inside 25:4-5) is bytes-accurate, but the row fails to disclose the same before-the-king echo into its own closing seam that the neighboring row discloses from the other side.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel הגו returns exactly 4 verses book-wide (16:33, 18:18, 25:4, 25:5), confirming the row's 'occurs nowhere else in this part' claim. But sweep.py --skel לפני shows Prov.25.5, Prov.25.6, and Prov.25.7 all three carrying the phrase, i.e. this row's own closing verse (25:5) shares the identical two-word phrase לפני + melekh with the very next verse (25:6) verbatim -- a byte-true device straddling this row's own seam that the campaign's cross-seam-cohesion rule requires disclosed at every row it touches. The row is silent on it even though the immediate neighbor row (25:6-7) states it. This does not overturn the cluster call -- the shift from this row's 3rd-person indefinite policy statement to the neighbor's 2nd-person direct admonition still separates them -- but the missing disclosure is a live defect under the standing symmetry rule.

items.claim: The 25:6-7 cluster's grammatical dependency is sound, and the row correctly discloses the before-the-king cross-seam echo into 25:5 rather than concealing it.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel לפני confirms the phrase recurs at all three of Prov.25.5/25.6/25.7 exactly as the row discloses. The shift from 25:4-5's 3rd-person indefinite policy statement (the הגו imperative, no direct address) to 25:6-7's 2nd-person direct admonition (the row's own cited prohibition plus 'your eyes have seen') is a real address-form boundary that outweighs the shared prepositional phrase and supports the row's choice not to adopt the echo into a merge; v7's motive clause is confirmed to have no referent independent of v6 by direct byte read.

items.claim: The single_proverb call at 25:8 is correctly defended: the shared token with 25:9 is verified too pervasive across the part (4 sites) to bound a two-verse cluster, exactly as the row states.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel רעך returns 9 verses book-wide; filtered to part P11 (25:1-27:27): Prov.25.8, Prov.25.9, Prov.25.17, Prov.27.10 -- exactly the 4 sites the row cites, confirming both the digit and the object (רעך/רעך skeleton match, pointing differs only by pausal accent, correctly treated as the same skeleton token).
